line: The alarm rings. What will today bring? Nobody knows. So start living now.
credit: Seneca · On the Shortness of Life 9.1

line: And live ready: the wise look ahead, so trouble cannot shake them.
credit: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 429, tr. G. U. Pope

line: How? Dancer Twyla Tharp's ritual wasn't the workout. It was getting into the taxi.
Two short, heavy lifting sessions a week improved weak bones in older women.
Eat just enough, keep regular hours, never overdo it: body and spirit stay together.
Relaxed face, calm full breath, soft muscles: where could tomorrow's worries get in?
credit: William James · The Gospel of Relaxation

line: Ayurveda's alarm clock: a healthy person rises before dawn, to protect a long life.
Then the same asanas daily: what felt impossible on Monday is normal by Saturday.
Train at a fixed hour, hot or cold, even when you'd rather not.
Set the alarm: regular practice eases stiffness, and morning practice helps you work better.
credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Yoga, 1966
